steps_h2: How to Make Virtual Try-On Photos in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Upload your garment, choose the model and scene, then download an on-model image for your listing.

steps.d: Upload a clear flat-lay or hanger photo that shows the full garment, including the collar and hem.
Choose the model and scene. Describe the pose while keeping the garment color and details true to your photo.
Download the on-model image and compare its fit, print, and fastenings with the garment you sell.

faq.q: What does virtual try-on make for my clothing store?
faq.a: It places your garment on an AI model in a still image. A clear flat-lay or hanger photo is enough to start.

faq.q: How do I make an on-model clothing photo?
faq.a: Upload a garment image, choose a model and scene, then review the fit and details before downloading.

faq.q: Which garments work for virtual try-on?
faq.a: Jackets, dresses, trousers, knitwear, and other wearable pieces work best when the whole garment is visible.

faq.q: Can I make several try-on images for one garment?
faq.a: Yes. Use the same garment photo for another pose or scene, then check each image against the real piece.

faq.q: Which clothing shops can use try-on photos?
faq.a: Independent shops, clothing labels, and agencies can make on-model images for listings and social ads.

faq.q: Can I use virtual try-on without editing experience?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the garment, choose a model, and download the image after checking the result.

faq.q: When can I download my try-on image?
faq.a: Download it after generation finishes and you have checked the garment color, shape, and details.

faq.q: What does a virtual try-on photo cost?
faq.a: One generated image costs 24 credits. You see the cost before starting. The [AI Instagram ads](page:plat-instagram) page covers square placements.
